A Colombia ELN hostage exchange has been ruled out by the country’s new president. Abelardo De la Espriella rejected the idea on Thursday 17 September 2026.

“There will be no swap. The lives and freedom of Colombians are not bargaining chips,” he said, in remarks carried by the Bucaramanga daily Vanguardia.

De la Espriella took office on 7 August 2026 in Cali, succeeding Gustavo Petro. He was elected on a hard-security platform and promised to fight illegal armed groups.

Who the ELN are

The Ejército de Liberación Nacional, or National Liberation Army, is a Marxist guerrilla group formed in 1964. It launched publicly on 7 January 1965 by seizing the town of Simacota.

That adds up to 62 years of continuous armed activity. InSight Crime, a research group that tracks organised crime in the region, calls it the last remaining guerrilla insurgency in Colombia.

Its founders fused Marxism-Leninism with liberation theology, and a Spanish priest, Manuel Pérez, later led it. That clerical strand still sets the ELN apart from the FARC.

InSight Crime puts its strength at roughly 6,300 people, fighters and support networks together. About a fifth of them are based in Venezuela.

The same profile counts a presence in at least 184 Colombian municipalities across 19 departments. The group is strongest along the Venezuelan border.

InSight Crime lists extortion, drug trafficking, illegal mining and kidnapping among its sources of money. Kidnapping is a revenue line, not an accident.

The four people being held

They were seized on 17 August 2026 on the Ocaña-Cúcuta road in Norte de Santander, near Venezuela. Three are officers of the DIJIN, the National Police’s judicial investigation directorate.

They are Major Fredy Alexis Russi González, Patrol Officer Erika Tatiana Monroy Hurtado and Patrol Officer Edinson Yesid Medina Traslaviña. The fourth captive is a civilian, Angi Jácome.

What the guerrillas actually said

The ELN confirmed it held the four in a communique dated 17 September 2026. It came with proof of life and said they were in good health.

A swap was raised only in passing, and the wording was conditional. Semana carried the line: “The possibility of regaining freedom, or a swap, is always a possibility the ELN values.”

No list of prisoners, no numbers and no names have been published. The ELN said the four would be held while it looked into alleged operations against it.

A round of Colombian government talks with the ELN, in a 2023 file photograph (Photo: Rio Times media library)

Why a canje is refused

A Colombia ELN hostage exchange, or canje, would trade captives for imprisoned fighters. De la Espriella refused, and the legal objection was set out before he took office.

The clearest official statement on the law predates this government. “A swap would imply recognising the legitimacy of an illegal armed group,” Jorge Iván Cuervo said in May 2026.

Cuervo, then justice minister under Petro, told the Barranquilla daily El Heraldo that neither international law nor Colombian legislation allowed it.

That was the previous government’s position. De la Espriella’s justice minister is Iván Cancino, named in the cabinet announced in August 2026.

The peace talks are over

Any exchange would need a channel, and none is open. On 11 September 2026 De la Espriella announced the dismantling of the ELN dialogue he inherited from Petro.

“The false peace is over,” he said, in remarks reported by the Bogotá magazine Semana. He had already cut dialogue with three other armed groups on 31 August 2026.

The ELN table was already suspended under Petro, the Latin American news service NODAL reported. Petro had frozen it for want of a demonstrated commitment to peace.

Semana reported that four years of ELN talks cost more than 7,000 million Colombian pesos, or about US$2.22 million, in fees.

That conversion uses the official TRM rate of 3,151.73 to the dollar. El Heraldo published that rate, Colombia’s official daily reference, on 18 September 2026.

The military track instead

What replaces dialogue is force. De la Espriella ordered military and police operations, running since the 17 August kidnapping, to be intensified.

He told the ELN to release the four “immediately, safe and sound, and without conditions”. He directed the forces to act within the constitution and the law.

His defence minister is retired army general Jorge Eduardo Mora López, whose appointment was announced in July 2026. The rejection of 17 September 2026 came from the president himself.

Two days before the communique, on 15 September 2026, troops freed eight people held by the ELN. Infobae said they had been held for nearly two years.

That rescue took place in rural parts of Convención, in the Catatumbo region near Venezuela. The army, the police, the air force and the Fiscalía, Colombia’s prosecution service, all took part.

Infobae reported that United States Southern Command and the US Drug Enforcement Administration supported the operation. Colonel Fabio Ojeda directs the police GAULA, the anti-kidnapping unit that went in.

GAULA stands for Grupo de Acción Unificada por la Libertad Personal. Major General José Bertulfo Soto Sánchez commands the National Army.

What happens next

The sequence matters. A rescue on 15 September, proof of life on 17 September, and a refusal the same day.

For the government, a swap would hand the group recognition it has sought for decades. Its stated route is rescue, not a deal.

Beyond these four captives, the group’s full tally of hostages is not publicly known. Agency reporting on 15 September 2026 said the exact figure was unknown.

For foreign residents and travellers, the geography is the practical point. Norte de Santander and the Catatumbo border strip are where the ELN is strongest.

More: Colombia coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the ELN?

The Ejército de Liberación Nacional, or National Liberation Army, is a Colombian guerrilla group formed in 1964 and launched publicly in January 1965. Its politics mix Marxism-Leninism with liberation theology, and a Spanish priest, Manuel Pérez, once led it. InSight Crime puts its strength at about 6,300 fighters and support members, roughly a fifth of them based in Venezuela, with a presence in at least 184 Colombian municipalities. InSight Crime calls it the last remaining guerrilla insurgency in Colombia.

What is a canje, and why did Colombia say no?

A canje is a swap: captives held by an armed group traded for its members held in prison. President Abelardo De la Espriella rejected the ELN offer on 17 September 2026, saying the lives and freedom of Colombians are not bargaining chips. The legal objection was put most clearly by Jorge Iván Cuervo, justice minister under Gustavo Petro, in May 2026. He told El Heraldo that a swap would imply recognising the legitimacy of an illegal armed group.

Are peace talks with the ELN still running?

No. On 11 September 2026 De la Espriella announced the dismantling of the ELN dialogue inherited from the Petro government, saying the false peace was over. He had already ended talks with three other armed groups on 31 August 2026. The ELN table had in any case been suspended under Petro, according to the news service NODAL. There is no negotiating channel open at the time of writing.

Who are the four people the ELN is holding?

Three are officers of the DIJIN, the National Police’s judicial investigation directorate: Major Fredy Alexis Russi González, Patrol Officer Erika Tatiana Monroy Hurtado and Patrol Officer Edinson Yesid Medina Traslaviña. The fourth is a civilian, Angi Jácome. They were taken on 17 August 2026 on the Ocaña-Cúcuta road in Norte de Santander. Infobae and Semana spell some of the names differently, including Freddy Russi, Edison Medina and Angie Jácome.

Sources: El Heraldo on the rejection and the four captives, Vanguardia on the president’s wording, Semana on the ELN communique, Infobae on the 17 August kidnapping, Semana on the end of the ELN dialogue, Infobae on the Catatumbo rescue, El Heraldo on the legal objection to a swap, InSight Crime on the ELN’s size and reach, Infobae on the cabinet, El Heraldo on the official peso rate

World.title: Brazil Supreme Court Refuses Search Warrant for Bahia Candidate
World.content:
Brazil · Politics

Key Facts — What happened Justice Kássio Nunes Marques refused a police request for a search warrant against ACM Neto, while authorising 24 others.

— Who he is Antônio Carlos Magalhães Neto, former mayor of Salvador, is the União Brasil candidate for governor of Bahia on 4 October 2026.

— Who the judge is Nunes Marques is the Supreme Court rapporteur supervising Operation Overclean, drawn to the inquiry in January 2025.

— The catch A refused warrant is not an acquittal. Overclean continues, the decision is sealed, and no charge against him has been announced.

— What he says ACM Neto says he has no relation with the facts under investigation, and calls the leaks an orchestrated action.

— A separate matter A Banco Master plea bargain naming him was rejected by both the federal police and the prosecutor-general.

The Nunes Marques ACM Neto decision refused one warrant. The same justice authorised 24 other searches in the same Operation Overclean phase on 17 September 2026.

The Justice statue outside the Supreme Federal Court in Brasília, where Justice Nunes Marques sits (Photo: Rio Times media library)

A Brazilian Supreme Court justice authorised 24 search warrants in a corruption inquiry on 17 September 2026. The Nunes Marques ACM Neto decision refused the one aimed at a candidate for governor.

Antônio Carlos Magalhães Neto, known as ACM Neto, is the União Brasil candidate for governor of Bahia. The northeastern state votes on 4 October 2026.

He is a former mayor of Salvador and his party’s national vice-president, and holds no elected office now.

Justice Kássio Nunes Marques supervises the whole investigation at the Supreme Federal Court. The office of the prosecutor-general had supported the refused request, Bahia Notícias reported.

The sweep the justice did approve

The warrants were executed on 17 September 2026, in Overclean’s tenth phase. They covered six states: Minas Gerais, Bahia, São Paulo, Tocantins, Paraná and Espírito Santo.

Those searched included Bruno Barral, the businessman José Marcos Moura and Alex Parente. Only the measure against ACM Neto was turned down.

The refusal became public that day, as the phase was executed. The decision is under seal, CNN Brasil reported, and its date is not public.

Bahia Notícias, citing the UOL columnist Natália Portinari, said the justice found no legal basis for the measure. His office declined to comment, Jornal Passaporte reported.

The police asked for the warrant early this year, before the electoral period, CNN Brasil reported. The prosecutor-general’s supporting opinion came then too.

What Operation Overclean is examining

Overclean is a federal police investigation into public money diverted through contracts and parliamentary amendments. Parliamentary amendments are funds that individual lawmakers direct to their home regions.

One strand concerns possible fraud in contracts signed in 2024 and 2025 by a municipal secretary in Belo Horizonte. That city is the capital of Minas Gerais.

Three of them together exceed R$80 million (about US$15.6 million) at the commercial rate of R$5.14 to US$1 on 18 September 2026. The police say the true total is higher, with other procurements still under examination.

The wider inquiry spans 2018 to 2024 across five states, Poder360 reported. It touches people connected to eight political parties.

The Pelourinho district of Salvador, the Bahian capital where ACM Neto was mayor. The photograph is a general view and is unconnected to the investigation (Photo: Rio Times media library)

What the police alleged about the candidate

In a sealed filing, the police said ACM Neto had indicated “the then education secretary of Salvador, Bruno Barral”. The post in question was the equivalent job in Belo Horizonte.

The purpose, in the police account, was “to close contracts with the investigated group”. They also cited “frequent contacts between ACM Neto and businessman José Marcos Moura”.

Barral was ACM Neto’s education secretary in Salvador from 2017 to 2020, then took the same post in Belo Horizonte. He was dismissed in April 2025, after an earlier Overclean phase.

CNN Brasil reported that the police treat ACM Neto as the principal subject in this phase, in a sealed filing. Brasil 247 confines that police label to the Belo Horizonte education-contracts front.

Why the case is at the Supreme Court

ACM Neto has no privileged forum of his own. The inquiry sits at the Supreme Court because of someone else.

Federal deputy Elmar Nascimento, of União Brasil, is covered by foro privilegiado. That rule sends cases touching sitting members of Congress to the top court.

Nunes Marques was drawn as rapporteur in January 2025. A rapporteur supervises the inquiry and rules on the measures the police request.

A refusal decides one investigative step, and is not an acquittal or a finding about the allegations.

Overclean continues, and the searches the justice approved went ahead. Being named as a subject of an inquiry is not a criminal charge.

The Banco Master allegations are a separate matter

A second set of claims has circulated in Bahia this month, from a different case entirely. It concerns Banco Master, whose former owner Daniel Vorcaro is held in pre-trial detention.

Vorcaro proposed a plea bargain naming ACM Neto and Antônio Rueda, O Povo reported on 11 September 2026. He alleged the two “received 10% of the values” that pension funds put into the bank.

That would imply up to R$200 million (about US$38.9 million) in commissions. He never specified payments actually made.

It was his third such proposal, and both the federal police and the prosecutor-general rejected it. A second had been rejected in June 2026.

They found it lacked new information and offered insufficient guarantees on returning assets. His defence asked the court to revoke his detention on 18 September 2026.

ACM Neto called those accusations “absurd, completely fantastical and lying”. Rueda said he had no access to the document and that his contracts were legitimate legal services.

Federal deputy Alice Portugal, of the PCdoB in Bahia, demanded an investigation on 10 September 2026. She cited the Banco Master claims and a reported payment of R$3.6 million (about US$700,000).

The warrant the justice refused belongs to Overclean, not to the Banco Master case. Robinson Almeida, a PT state deputy in Bahia, linked the two publicly after the request emerged.

What ACM Neto said

ACM Neto issued written statements on 17 and 18 September 2026, carried by CNN Brasil, O Povo and Poder360. He described an “orchestrated action” to interfere in the elections.

“The courts prevented a new episode of this plot from prospering,” he said, affirming his “clean campaign”.

In a written note he said he had “no relation with the investigated facts”. The decision, he said, showed the “inconsistency” of police suspicions.

Júlio Pinheiro, a PT candidate for state deputy and former mayor of Amargosa, wants him to waive bank and tax secrecy. “If there is nothing to hide, open the seals,” he said.

What it means before the vote

Bahia chooses a governor on 4 October 2026, and the inquiry did not end with the refusal. The judge declined one measure, and made no finding on guilt or innocence.

More: Brazil coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is ACM Neto?

Antônio Carlos Magalhães Neto, universally called ACM Neto, is a former mayor of Salvador and national vice-president of União Brasil. He holds no elected office and is a candidate for governor of Bahia in the election of 4 October 2026. CNN Brasil reported that the federal police treat him as the principal subject in this phase of Operation Overclean, in a filing that remains sealed. He says he has no relation with the facts under investigation.

Does the refusal mean ACM Neto is cleared?

No. A refused search warrant is a ruling that one investigative measure did not meet the legal threshold. It is not an acquittal, not a dismissal of the case, and not a finding about the allegations. The same justice authorised 24 other searches in the same phase, Operation Overclean continues, and no criminal charge against him has been announced.

What is Operation Overclean?

It is a federal police investigation into public money diverted through contracts and parliamentary amendments, now in its tenth phase. One strand concerns contracts signed by a municipal secretary in Belo Horizonte in 2024 and 2025, three of which together exceed R$80 million (about US$15.6 million), with the police saying the true total is higher. The inquiry spans 2018 to 2024 across five states and touches people connected to eight political parties. The tenth phase was executed on 17 September 2026 in six states.

Is this the Banco Master case?

No. The warrant refused in the Nunes Marques ACM Neto decision was sought in Operation Overclean. The Banco Master claims came from a proposed plea bargain by Daniel Vorcaro, the bank’s former owner, who is held in pre-trial detention; O Povo reported the proposal on 11 September 2026. It was his third, and both the federal police and the prosecutor-general rejected it for lacking new information and for insufficient guarantees on returning assets. ACM Neto called the accusations absurd and lying.

World.title: Brazil Finance Minister Pledges Lower Debt Than His Own Budget Shows
World.content:
Brazil · Economy

Key Facts — What happened The Dário Durigan public debt pledge is that debt reaches 2030 below 80% of GDP, without saying which measure.

— The catch Only the gross measure makes that pledge meaningful. The government’s own budget bill projects gross debt at 87.5% for 2030.

— Where debt stands now Gross general government debt reached 82.5% of GDP in July 2026. The narrower net measure was 69.1%.

— Who holds the office Brazil’s finance minister is Dário Carnevalli Durigan, 42, in post since March 2026, after Fernando Haddad left to run for governor.

— Why it matters Debt rose 3.9 points of GDP in the year to July 2026. Nominal interest added 5.7 points, more than the net rise.

— Who is affected Bolsa Família benefits rise 15% from October 2026, lifting the minimum payment to R$691, about US$134.

Brazil’s finance minister says debt will reach 2030 below 80% of economic output, without saying which measure. The government’s own budget guidelines bill projects 87.5%.

The Esplanada dos Ministérios in Brasília at dusk, where the finance ministry sits (Photo: Marcelo Trad, Rio Times media library)

Brazil’s finance minister says the country’s debt will fall below 80% of economic output by 2030. The Dário Durigan public debt pledge sits well below the government’s own published projection.

The minister is Dário Carnevalli Durigan, 42, in the job since March 2026. He took over from Fernando Haddad, who left to run for governor of São Paulo.

Durigan made the remarks in one interview with the Brazilian news portal UOL, published on Friday 18 September 2026.

The pledge, in his own words

“In fact, I did not want it to go above 80% of GDP,” he said. “But we will get to 2030 below 80% of GDP.”

He then added a third clause, which loosens the pledge from below 80% to around it. “Or at least at 80% of GDP.”

Jornal do Comércio and O Povo both headlined the remark as citing a level of 80% for 2030. Durigan also said the trajectory “bothers us” and that growth stabilises from 2029, falling in 2030.

Gross debt is already above that line

Gross general government debt stood at 82.5% of GDP in July 2026. That was R$10.947 trillion, about US$2.13 trillion, in central bank figures released on 31 August 2026.

Conversions here use the commercial dollar rate of R$5.14 to US$1, its close on 18 September 2026 as reported by InfoMoney.

Gross debt to GDP measures what the federal government, the states, the municipalities and the social security fund owe. It is set against one year of national output.

No Brazilian law fixes 80% as a limit. It is a round marker that the minister used as his own test.

July’s reading is the highest since April 2021, when it stood at 82.62%. Net public sector debt, a narrower measure, was 69.1% of GDP, about US$1.78 trillion.

Durigan did not say which measure he meant. Below 80% only tests the gross figure, since the net one is already under it.

Interest is what moves the number. Over twelve months to July 2026 debt rose 3.9 points of GDP, with nominal interest alone adding 5.7 points.

The ministry buildings in Brasília, where the finance ministry set out the cost of the higher Bolsa Família floor (Photo: Rio Times media library)

What the government’s own bill projects

Each year the Ministry of Planning and Budget sends Congress a budget guidelines bill, known as the PLDO. It sets the fiscal targets and projections the next year’s budget must follow.

That ministry is separate from Durigan’s own Ministry of Finance. The bill of 15 April 2026 projects gross debt at 83.6% of GDP this year and 86.0% in 2027.

It then sees 87.3% in 2028, a peak of 87.8% in 2029, and 87.5% in 2030. Those figures were reported by CNN Brasil.

A National Treasury report of 30 June 2026 put the peak at 87.9% in 2029 and this year’s level at 83.5%.

So the Dário Durigan public debt target for 2030 sits about 7.5 points below the government’s own 87.5% projection. Neither the minister nor the outlets carrying the interview addressed the gap.

Bolsa Família and the 15% rise

Bolsa Família is Brazil’s main cash transfer programme, paying a monthly benefit to low-income families. President Lula announced a 15% increase on 17 September 2026, effective from October.

The minimum benefit rises from R$600 to R$691, about US$117 to US$134. The average payment goes from R$675 to R$777, about US$131 to US$151.

Planning Minister Bruno Moretti said the INPC price index had risen 15.04% since the programme’s 2023 relaunch, to August. That makes it a catch-up with inflation, not a real increase.

The minister said there was “no incompatibility” between the increase and fiscal responsibility.

He said it fits the 2026 budget, Correio Braziliense reported, and contrasted it with past extraordinary credit measures. ICL Notícias put the cost at R$5.8 billion this year, about US$1.13 billion.

The R$117 billion figure, explained

A widely repeated number puts R$117.1 billion, about US$22.8 billion, of Bolsa Família spending on the public debt. It is not a loan taken out for the new increase.

It is a calculation by Estadão, reported by A Crítica de Campo Grande. That share is about 18% of a R$649.4 billion outlay, around US$126.3 billion, across 2023 to 2026.

The Federal Senate has its own non-partisan watchdog, the Independent Fiscal Institution. It projects a 2027 primary deficit, against the government’s projected surplus of R$18.6 billion, about US$3.62 billion.

Buying up old household debts

In the same interview Durigan set out a plan for the National Treasury to buy aged household debts from creditors. It would target debts that lenders already treat as unrecoverable.

The Treasury would buy them at deep discounts, then either keep collecting while offering consumers reductions, or forgive them. “It is possible that this debt could be bought at a discount of 95% or more,” he said.

Durigan said the proposal goes to President Lula and should take effect from early next year. He put the timing down to the auction process and its procedural steps.

The news site Sem Pauta News headlined that 2027 start against the general election on 4 October 2026. The electoral reading came from the press, not from the minister.

Why the fiscal framework does not settle it

Brazil replaced its rigid 2016 spending cap with a system called the new fiscal framework. It sets an annual primary result target and ties spending growth to revenue growth.

The primary result is the budget balance before interest is paid. That is the gap the rules control, and interest sits outside them.

So a government can meet every target and still watch debt climb. CNN Brasil reported a study finding the budget complies while keeping a structural deficit.

The Treasury has warned the 2026 to 2028 targets will be missed without a revenue effort. That is the test the minister’s pledge now faces.

More: Brazil coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Brazil’s finance minister?

The Minister of Finance is Dário Carnevalli Durigan, aged 42. He was chosen by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and has held the post since March 2026. He replaced Fernando Haddad, who left the ministry to run for governor of São Paulo. Durigan was still in office on 18 September 2026, the day the UOL interview was published.

What does gross debt to GDP measure?

It compares what the federal government, the states, the municipalities and the social security fund owe with one year of national economic output. Brazil’s gross general government debt was 82.5% of GDP in July 2026, or R$10.947 trillion, about US$2.13 trillion. A narrower measure, net public sector debt, was 69.1%. The 80% mark is not a legal limit; it is a round marker that ministers and analysts use as shorthand.

What is Bolsa Família?

It is Brazil’s main cash transfer programme, paying a monthly benefit to low-income families. President Lula announced a 15% increase on 17 September 2026, effective from October. The minimum benefit rises from R$600 to R$691, about US$117 to US$134, and the average payment from R$675 to R$777, about US$131 to US$151. A Crítica de Campo Grande reported that the money comes from reallocation inside the budget bill before Congress, without expanding the overall spending limit.

What would the household debt buy-back do?

The National Treasury would buy old household debts from banks and other creditors at a steep discount, possibly 95% or more. It would then either keep collecting while offering consumers reductions, or forgive the debts outright. Durigan said the proposal is going to President Lula and should start early in 2027, with the delay caused by auction rules and procedural steps. No programme size has been announced.

World.title: Video of Costa Rica’s 119-Year-Old Man Making a Bid to Be Oldest Ever
World.content:
José Flores Flores, the Guanacaste farmer who turned 119 in July, is now at the center of a formal effort to have him recognized as the oldest man in recorded history. The Asociación Península de Nicoya Zona Azul, a group that promotes the Nicoya Peninsula’s reputation for long life, is preparing his case for Guinness World Records.

Its president, Jorge Vindas, said the association is still waiting on two documents needed for the application. He did not say what they are. Flores’ national identity card lists his birth as July 11, 1907, in Las Lajas de Cañas, Guanacaste. That date has not been validated by Guinness or by any of the international organizations that specialize in verifying extreme ages.

Those bodies typically require records from different stages of a person’s life that can be tied to the same individual. If the documents hold up, the numbers are remarkable. Guinness recognizes Japan’s Jiroemon Kimura, who died in 2013 at 116 years and 54 days, as the oldest man ever verified. Flores’ documented age already exceeds Kimura’s by more than two and a half years.

The oldest living man Guinness recognizes is Brazil’s João Marinho Neto, who turns 114 on Oct. 5. The oldest living person is British woman Ethel Caterham, who turned 117 in August. Only three people in history have verified lifespans longer than Flores’ current documented age. France’s Jeanne Calment died in 1997 at 122 years and 164 days.

AFP Video of Costa Rica’s Oldest Man

Japan’s Kane Tanaka reached 119 years and 107 days, and American Sarah Knauss reached 119 years and 97 days. By his papers, Flores would pass Knauss on Oct. 17 and Tanaka on Oct. 27. His case has drawn attention at the highest level. President Laura Fernández visited Flores in July and ordered a new home built for him, one suited to someone of his age, according to AFP.

Flores lives with relatives in Sardinal de Carrillo, on the Nicoya Peninsula, and now gets around with a walker. His granddaughter, Hellen Flores, told AFP he stays active in the afternoons. He plays dominoes with the family, watches his programs and naps in his chair. She said his treatment is limited to two pills and some drops for his prostate and heart, and that he still has the occasional whisky.

At 105, she said, he was still dancing, carrying a machete and heading out to do chores. She described a lively youth that included parties, smoking, drinking and boxing. Flores worked on a banana plantation and as a farmer. His granddaughter credits his diet and the care of his family for his long life.

According to his granddaughter, Flores has been a widower for 23 years. He had eight children, one of whom has died. Flores himself, speaking with some difficulty, said God was the secret to his long life. His advice to young people was to work the way he did.

He has not lost his loyalties either as for his birthday, his soccer club, Liga Deportiva Alajuelense, gave him a jersey bearing the number 119. Sardinal lies in one of the world’s five Blue Zones, regions where longevity researchers have found people living unusually long, healthy lives. Several residents of the Nicoya Peninsula have passed 100.

Whether Flores enters the record books now depends on paperwork older than most of the 20th century. Until the documents are accepted, he remains a claimant rather than a verified record holder. If they hold, he will have outlived every man whose age has ever been confirmed.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Juan Santamaría Airport Keeps Highest Passenger Experience Accreditation
World.content:
Costa Rica’s Juan Santamaría International Airport has renewed the highest level of an international passenger experience accreditation, placing the country’s main airport among just 12 worldwide holding the distinction in 2026. The airport, operated by AERIS, received Level 5 accreditation for the second consecutive year under the Airports Council International Customer Experience Accreditation program. Level 5 is the highest of five levels in the program.

The distinction does not simply rank airports based on how much passengers like them. Instead, ACI examines how well an airport has built the passenger experience into the way it operates, including how it listens to travelers, trains employees, measures service, uses technology and coordinates the different companies and government agencies working inside the terminal.

Juan Santamaría is one of only 12 airports worldwide currently holding Level 5 accreditation. Quito’s Mariscal Sucre International Airport in Ecuador is the other Level 5 airport in the Americas. “Renewing Level 5 represents for us an achievement as important as reaching it for the first time, because it demonstrates that we have managed to maintain a culture of service over time and that the passenger experience is part of the decisions we make to continue transforming the airport,” AERIS CEO Ricardo Hernández said.

AERIS has expanded its passenger service programs over the past year, including an Excellence Program aimed at improving customer service across the airport community. The airport also strengthened its Customer Experience Committee, which brings together airlines, airport operators, businesses and government agencies to identify problems and coordinate improvements.

About 500 employees from AERIS and other organizations working at Juan Santamaría participated in training, workshops and passenger service activities during 2025. Travelers have also begun seeing more technology designed to reduce waiting times and make moving through the terminal easier.

The airport is using LiDAR technology to anonymously monitor passenger flows around passport control and security in the international departures area. According to AERIS, Juan Santamaría is the first airport in Latin America to use the technology for this purpose. Other projects include automated eGates for immigration, self-service baggage drop systems and new scanning technology at security checkpoints. The airport began operating its first four eGates in the arrivals area on September 8.

Accessibility has also become part of the effort. Juan Santamaría joined the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower program, an international system that allows travelers with non-visible disabilities to discreetly signal that they may need extra time or assistance. The airport has also achieved Level 1 in ACI’s Accessibility Enhancement Accreditation program.

Recent passenger surveys indicate that the changes are being noticed. At the end of June 2026, Juan Santamaría scored 4.44 out of 5 for overall passenger satisfaction and 4.38 for overall experience under ACI’s Airport Service Quality program. Its satisfaction score was slightly above the worldwide average of 4.38 for airports handling a similar number of passengers.

The accreditation comes as Juan Santamaría continues a broader modernization program. The airport currently connects Costa Rica with 42 destinations and is served by 26 international airlines and two domestic carriers. For travelers, the Level 5 renewal does not mean every trip through Juan Santamaría will be trouble-free.

Lines, flight disruptions and busy travel periods remain part of airport travel. What the accreditation indicates is that passenger experience has become part of the airport’s formal management system rather than a collection of individual customer service projects. For Costa Rica, that carries added importance because Juan Santamaría is the first and last impression of the country for millions of international visitors each year.

World.title: Video of Orcas Spotted Near Costa Rica’s Cocos Island in Rare Encounter
World.content:
A group of orcas has been spotted near Costa Rica’s Cocos Island, giving park rangers a rare look at one of the ocean’s most recognizable predators in waters where the species is only occasionally reported. Between four and five orcas were observed around midday yesterday near Manuelita Islet, just off Cocos Island.

Park rangers found them while carrying out routine monitoring in the waters surrounding Cocos Island National Park. Several of the orcas appeared to be juveniles, raising the possibility that the animals were traveling as part of a family group. The encounter was captured on video.

While orcas can travel enormous distances and have previously been documented in Costa Rican waters, they are not considered regular visitors around Cocos Island. The remote national park is much better known for marine species that are routinely encountered there, including hammerhead sharks, whale sharks, manta rays and dolphins.

Scientific records show just how unusual an orca encounter around the island can be. A study examining Costa Rican Pacific sightings between 1990 and 2020 identified 31 reported orca encounters involving 105 animals throughout the country’s Pacific waters. Only four of those sightings, involving a total of 10 animals, were recorded around Cocos Island.

The South Pacific accounted for the largest number during the study period, with 17 sightings involving 56 animals. Researchers have not established that the latest appearance represents any broader change in the distribution of orcas around Costa Rica. Orcas are highly mobile animals capable of traveling long distances while searching for food. Their movements can be influenced by prey availability as well as changing ocean conditions.

The waters surrounding Cocos Island provide an unusually rich marine environment. Ocean currents and underwater mountains help concentrate nutrients and marine life around the island, supporting large populations of fish and other animals that can potentially attract top predators.

Orcas are opportunistic hunters with diets that vary significantly between populations. Depending on where they live and the group involved, they can feed on fish, rays, sharks, sea turtles and marine mammals. Their presence in Costa Rica is not unprecedented.

Occasional sightings have been documented for decades along the country’s Pacific coast, with previous reports occurring in the northern, central and southern Pacific as well as around Cocos Island. However, researchers still know relatively little about the orcas that pass through tropical waters compared with populations studied in areas such as the Pacific Northwest, Norway and Antarctica.

That makes individual sightings potentially useful for understanding when the animals appear in Costa Rican waters and where they travel. The latest encounter also highlights the extraordinary marine biodiversity surrounding Cocos Island, located approximately 550 kilometers (342 miles) off Costa Rica’s Pacific coast.

Its isolation and surrounding protected waters have made the island one of Costa Rica’s most important marine conservation areas and an internationally known destination for experienced divers.

For now, yesterday’s encounter appears to be another uncommon visit rather than evidence that orcas are becoming regular residents around the island. But for the park rangers conducting their routine monitoring, it provided a rare encounter with a species that can pass through Costa Rican waters without being seen for long periods.

World.title: Scientists Name First New Wild Cat Species in Over 100 Years
World.content:
A small spotted wild cat from the cloud forests of Bolivia has been formally described as a new species. Scientists say it is the first time in more than a century that a new living feline species has been formally named and described. The cat, now called Leopardus tilcayo, was described in a study published on Thursday in the journal Current Biology. Its name comes from tilcayo, the word local communities in Bolivia have long used for the animal.

It is smaller than a house cat and the species measures 46cm (18 inches) long and weighs about 1.4kg (3 pounds). Researchers describe light brown fur with irregularly shaped rosettes across its body. The tilcayo belongs to the tiger cats, small, wild cats in the Leopardus genus native to South and Central America. It lives in the Bolivian Yungas, the cloud forest where the Andes mountains meet the Amazon basin.

The discovery began with one cat at a wildlife sanctuary. In 2016, Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, a biologist and National Geographic Explorer working in Bolivia, received a call from a local wildlife sanctuary that had just been given what they described as “a weird cat.” The animal came from a local man who found it as a kitten on a road near a forest and kept it at home for about a year before realizing it was wild.

The cat went to the Senda Verde Wildlife Sanctuary as Nogales-Ascarrunz first assumed it was a northern tiger cat, a species described back in 1775 from a single illustration of an animal seen in French Guiana and long thought to live across Central and South America.

National Geographic

Her doubts grew in 2019 as while she was preparing a booklet about Bolivia’s cat species, she realized the cat she’d photographed didn’t look like a guidebook reference photo from neighboring Brazil. That led to a large genetic study and the team analyzed DNA from 38 cats sampled across several South American countries, including eight museum specimens and found that tiger cats are really five genetically distinct species.

Co-lead author Jonas Lescroart, an evolutionary ecologist at the University of Antwerp in Belgium, said the team never expected the Bolivian cat to be a separate species, and no one had ever proposed it as a different animal, subspecies or otherwise. He described tiger cats as “cryptic species,” meaning it is difficult to distinguish them by appearance alone.

Scientists believe the tilcayo cat likely evolved from a common ancestor of “tiger cats” around 1.4 million years ago. The same study also identified a subspecies of another tiger cat species, named Leopardus tigrinus antisuyo, which lives in Peru.

Much about the new species remains unknown. Lescroart said the team’s information is limited to the two live individuals that we examined, and a small number of camera-trap records. Rodent remains in scat samples hint at its diet, and camera-trap evidence suggests the cats are more active at night.

The sanctuary cat, a 10-year-old male at the sanctuary is the only known tilcayo cat in captivity, but others are believed to have been photographed by camera traps placed in the cloud forests. The researchers say the finding raises urgent conservation questions. Tadeu de Oliveira, a co-author and ecologist at the State University of Maranhão in Brazil, said all five tiger cat species are in habitats that are vanishing fast.

Nogales-Ascarrunz said naming a new cat after more than 100 years shows how much remains to be learned about nearby biodiversity, and that it underlines the need to protect the Yungas forests, which are home to so many species—including some we are only beginning to understand.

World.title: 62-year-old Belizean-American charged for allegedly breaking locks to 85-year-old dad’s house
World.content:
62-year-old Belizean-American charged for allegedly breaking locks to 85-year-old dad’s house

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A family dispute between an 85-year-old father and his 62-year-old son escalated into criminal proceedings on Friday, with the son taken before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on a charge of damage to property.

Evan Delsworth Grenwich Wade, described as a retired veteran who spends time between California and Belize, was arraigned after his father, Carl Wade, accused him of damaging locks at his Keating Crescent home in Buttonwood Bay.

Wade is accused of damaging two padlocks and two deadbolt locks valued at a total of $130 on Thursday, September 17.

Represented by attorney Bryan Neal, Wade pleaded not guilty and was granted bail of $300 plus one surety in the same amount. His next court appearance is scheduled for November 18, 2026.

According to the complaint made to police, Carl Wade had gone to the Belize Family Court a day earlier seeking a protection order against his son amid ongoing family disagreements, but his application was reportedly unsuccessful.

The elder Wade subsequently had several locks at his property changed. Police were later called to the residence when Wade’s grandson arrived, and the grandson reportedly packed his belongings and voluntarily left.

Carl Wade told police that he stayed elsewhere that night after being advised to do so. The following morning, he was informed that his son was at the residence.

When police and Carl Wade returned to the property, five locks were reportedly found damaged.

Carl also alleged that several personal items were missing from inside the house, including two passports, two sets of land documents, a vehicle certificate and cash. Police processed the scene and recorded a statement from the 85-year-old, who requested court action.

Following the investigation, Evan Wade was charged with one count of damage to property. Despite allegations concerning missing items from the home, the court information provided indicates that no burglary or theft charge was read to Wade at Friday’s arraignment.

Attorney Neal told the court that while Wade had been staying at his father’s home to assist in caring for him, he normally resides in Dangriga.

World.title: Man’s drivers license disqualified for 1 year; fined $700 for reckless driving and failing to provide urine sample – Says he didn’t have to pee at the time
World.content:
Man’s drivers license disqualified for 1 year; fined $700 for reckless driving and failing to provide urine sample – Says he didn’t have to pee at the time

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 45-year-old IT manager has been fined a total of $700, plus court costs, and disqualified from driving for one year after pleading guilty to reckless driving and failure to provide a specimen.

Lee Liu, a resident of Sandhill, appeared before Senior Magistrate Mannon Dennison in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, where he pleaded guilty to both traffic offences.

The charges stemmed from an incident around 5:10 a.m. on Thursday, September 17, when police officers conducting a checkpoint on the Philip Goldson Highway reportedly noticed a white car swerving across the highway.

A police constable signalled the driver to stop and, according to the prosecution’s facts, observed that Liu appeared intoxicated, had difficulty standing and was speaking with slurred speech. Police said Liu admitted that he had been drinking, telling the officer, “Yes, but I just want to go home.”

Liu was taken to a police station and initially agreed to provide a urine specimen for alcohol analysis. Police alleged that when the time came to provide the sample, however, Liu refused, saying he no longer wanted to give it.

In court, Liu explained that he had been driving around potholes on the highway, which he said accounted for the manner in which he was driving. Regarding the urine sample, he told the court that he did not feel the need to urinate at the time.

He was fined $500 plus $5 court costs for failure to provide a specimen, payable by November 30, 2026, or three months’ imprisonment in default. For reckless driving, Liu was fined $200 plus $5 court costs, payable by October 31, 2026, or two months’ imprisonment in default.

Liu was also disqualified from driving for one year, effective September 18, 2026. Belize’s Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic Act provides that a person who, without reasonable excuse, fails to provide a required blood or urine specimen commits an offence and, upon conviction, is subject to a 12-month disqualification from holding or obtaining a Belize driving licence.

When ordered to surrender his driver’s licence, Liu told the court that he did not have it with him and believed he had misplaced it at home. Senior Magistrate Dennison ordered him to surrender the licence at the Sandhill Police Station by 5:00 p.m. Friday.

He may apply in writing after 90 days seeking to have his driving privileges reinstated.

World.title: Bulridge Belize hiring full time Sales Representative in Georgeville
World.content:
Bulridge Belize hiring full time Sales Representative in Georgeville
