World.title: “Forever Chemicals” Found in Lika Water Following Waste Scandal
World.content:
September the 19th, 2026 – So-called “forever chemicals” have unfortunately been found in Lika water following the shameful hazardous waste scandal.

The Croatian Institute of Public Health (HZJZ) and the Public Health Institute of Lika-Senj County have published the results of extraordinary water sampling in the Lika area. Index reports that the results have revealed that dangerous PFAS compounds, so-called “forever chemicals,” were found in two private wells downstream from an illegal waste dump near Gospić, but they assure the public that the pollution is exclusively of a local character and that water from the public water supply is not endangered.

the chemicals were found in two wells near the illegal waste dump

According to the HZJZ statement, from the 20th of August to the 9th of September water was sampled from 43 private facilities – 38 wells, three cisterns and two springs. The Institute states that in one well in the immediate vicinity of the dump a concentration of PFAS compounds of 0.3018 µg/L was recorded, which is three times higher than the maximum permitted limit of 0.1 µg/L. In the second well 0.0265 µg/L was measured, which is within the permitted limits. HZJZ claims that the owners of the disputed wells are connected to the public water supply and do not use that water for drinking. As for the other findings, the Institute claims that in 33 facilities only “usual microbiological pollution characteristic of untreated water” was recorded, while elevated physical-chemical values in a further 10 samples are attributed to the natural properties of the karst, and not to the dumped waste.

the people of lika feel betrayed by the government

The statement comes at a moment when the scandal surrounding the illegal burial of as many as 37,000 tonnes of hazardous waste in Divoselo and Benkovačko Selo near Gospić has grown into a first-class political scandal. HZJZ Director Krunoslav Capak personally sits on the newly established Scientific Council of Prime Minister Andrej Plenković, a body that the government formed precisely with the aim of “correctly interpreting” in public the dramatic findings of the USKOK investigation into the pollution of soil and waters in Lika. The documents that Plenković’s Scientific Council is supposed to put into the “correct context” were signed by authorised institutions and are quite exact.

The expert examination by the “Josip Juraj Strossmayer” Water Institute for the Divoselo location established that the water passing immediately under the dump carries 89 percent of the total detected plastic, while upstream it is clean. 737 micrograms of Styrofoam per litre were measured, and the presence of Teflon from the group of “forever chemicals” (PFAS) was also recorded, with the expert’s note that the Lika River is a directly connected water body.

the prime minister is at the council’s helm

Although formally composed of professors from technical and natural science faculties, the Council has been placed under the direct authority of the Prime Minister. According to the government decision, the sessions are convened and chaired by Plenković himself, operational tasks are carried out by his office, and there are no prescribed obligations for the publication of minutes, expert conclusions or any dissenting opinions of members. The entire manoeuvre of forming the Council is taking place at a time when the remediation is only being prepared, and political pressure on the ruling party is growing after a mass protest in Zagreb and a drop in HDZ’s rating.

is there any real reason to panic?

Despite this, HZJZ persists in the claim that there is no reason for panic. They state that the fact that such compounds were not found in other wells across the county proves that it is “pollution of a local character in a narrower circle.” They also repeat that private wells in any case do not fall under regular state supervision and that the responsibility lies with the owners themselves. The Institute finally states that all regular tests confirm that water from the public water supply in the entire Lika-Senj County area, as well as on the islands of Pag and Rab, is completely health-safe and that they will continue monitoring the situation on the ground.

World.title: New Passenger and Hospitality Complex Coming to Split Port
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – A brand new passenger and hospitality complex is coming to Split Port, finally giving the entire area a much needed proverbial facelift.

What was once the Dalmacijavino winery, a work by architect Stanko Fabris and a gem of Croatian modern architecture, has over time become a dilapidated, abandoned building in what is definitely one of the most beautiful locations in the entire city. A place where Katalinića brig meets the port, the sea, and the rest of the world.

Morski reports that the Split Port Authority, the manager of that part of the port, has received a permit for the changes. After more than two years of waiting, the Split Port Authority has finally obtained a location permit – a permit for the changes according to which the building will be repurposed, under strict conservation guidelines. The building is under the protection of the Conservation Department of the Ministry of Culture.

After all the necessary studies (economic and legal) in cooperation with the constituents of the University of Split, and according to conservation guidelines, we conducted an international expression of interest from potential concessionaires and submitted all the necessary documentation to the City of Split, and we finally have it.

As part of the city’s project for the arrangement of Split’s Eastern Coast, according to the existing city Master Plan (GUP), two garages with 500 parking spaces can be built at that location, which would solve the problem of stationary traffic in the city port; passenger space can be expanded, accompanying hospitality facilities, and even a hotel with around a hundred rooms.

Now that the location permit has arrived, an international tender will be announced for the concession of the building and the space around it. The significance of this investment can best be shown through numbers, and that is the estimated value of the concession, which totals a massive 600,000,000 euros.

World.title: New Croatian Price Comparison System Coming Next Month
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – A brand new Croatian price comparison system is coming next month, with additional technical obligations awaiting traders and service providers.

As of the 1st of October 2026 in Croatia, the prices highlighted on the shelves, in the menus or on the price lists will no longer stand alone. Poslovni reports that alongside the current price an additional, so-called anchor price will also have to be stated. The new obligation applies to all retailers and registered service providers in Croatia. This means that the new rules will not cover only supermarkets, but also clothing and footwear shops, technical goods, furniture and building materials stores, as well as restaurants, cafes, hair and beauty salons, car mechanics, various service workshops and other craftsmen who offer their products or services to consumers.

The anchor price will be the regular price that applied to a particular product or service on 10 September 2026, without promotions, discounts and other special forms of sale. A hair salon will thus have to state, alongside the current price of a haircut or colouring, also the price of the same service on that date; a car mechanic will have to do the same alongside the price of a working hour or a particular service; and a restaurant alongside the prices of food and drinks in the menu or price list.

The anchor price is neither frozen nor the highest permitted price. A trader or craftsman can still change prices, but the consumer will at any moment be able to see how much the current price differs from the one that applied on the 10th of September, explain lawyers Dora Ljevar and Danijel Pribanić. The obligation also applies when advertising prices. If a trader or service provider publishes a price on a leaflet, poster, digital , outdoor advertising space or website, they will also have to highlight the anchor price alongside it. An exception applies to traders who for food, drinks, cosmetics, cleaning agents, toiletries and household products already had to highlight an additional price. For those products the relevant price remains the one that applied on the 2nd of May 2025.

Additional technical obligations await traders and service providers who already have their own website. On it they will have to publish a price list in XML or CSV format, which enables the automatic collection and comparison of data. Traders will update the price list every working day by 08:00 at the latest, and service providers after every price change, also 08:00 on the day of the change at the latest. Previously published price lists will have to remain available for 30 days. Those who do not have their own website are not obliged to set one up solely because of this obligation. Traders and craftsmen should therefore keep proof of the prices that applied on the 10th of September and, by the start of application of the new rules, adapt the price lists in business premises, s and websites.

World.title: Croatia’s Zvijezda Marks 110 Years of Successful Business
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – Croatia’s famous brand Zvijezda has celebrated 110 years of doing successful business and engaging in market leadership.

Zvijezda mayonnaise and Zvijezda oil occupy first and second place on the ranking of the strongest brands in Croatia according to Ipsos research. Poslovni reports that the very well known Zvijezda, a market leader and Croatian manufacturing company whose values are founded on tradition, quality and innovativeness, celebrated 110 years of successful business.

The ceremony was held at the Zagreb City Museum, on the day when in 1916 the First Croatian Oil Factory was founded in Zagreb, in the presence of numerous company partners as well as representatives of institutions and the media. Zvijezda’s strong position is also confirmed by data on the habits of Croatian households: every second edible oil used in Croatia is Zvijezda’s, two out of three cakes are baked with Zvijezda margarine, and nine out of ten people, when it comes to mayonnaise, first think of Zvijezda.

According to the BRANDpuls research by the Ipsos agency from spring 2026, as many as five Zvijezda brands are among the 20 strongest brands on the Croatian market, with Zvijezda mayonnaise and Zvijezda oil occupying the first two places.

“I’m proud that we’re the market leader in almost all categories in which we have decided to compete, and the historically high result in the mayonnaise category of more than 70 percent confirms this. Zvijezda has for years been the number 1 brand among all brands of fast-moving consumer goods, and we continuously achieve these results thanks to our consumers, employees and partners,” emphasised Dinko Jurišić, member of the Management Board of Zvijezda. From the very beginnings of production in the First Croatian Oil Factory right up to the present day, the company has over the decades followed the needs of consumers, developed new products and set standards for the domestic food industry.

As such, back in 1956, it became the first producer of margarine in the country, in 1959 it introduced mayonnaise to the market, and in 2016 it launched the production of its own ketchup. The company today operates through the brands Zvijezda, Margo and Omegol. “Today, Zvijezda is a large and modern company, which is best proven by these figures: €150 million in annual revenue, more than 400 employees and presence on more than 15 markets. We look at these 110 years with pride, but even more with a sense of responsibility towards what is coming, therefore we continue to invest in the development of our products, the modernisation of production, the digitalisation of processes and sustainable solutions that will further strengthen Zvijezda’s competitiveness,” stated at the ceremony Karmen Rosan, member of the Management Board of Zvijezda.

Since this year Zvijezda has been operating as part of the Žito Group, one of the leading Croatian food groups. By entering the Žito Group a new development chapter has begun for Zvijezda, directed towards further strengthening of business, market position and the creation of new opportunities for growth.

“Zvijezda is one of the best-known Croatian food brands and a company that for 110 years has had a special place in the lives of generations of consumers. Its entry into the Žito Group represents a great responsibility for us, but also an opportunity to jointly build a new chapter of one of the most successful Croatian business stories, so that in the years to come we remain competitive and recognisable among consumers,” said Josip Bičvić, President of the Supervisory Board of Zvijezda. Zvijezda marked the anniversary also with a donation to the Croatian Down Syndrome Association, with which it has been cooperating for more than ten years, and as part of the cooperation the labels of a special edition of Zvijezda sunflower oil were decorated with drawings by children from the Association.

World.title: Croatian Scientists Concerned by Adriatic Sea Test Results
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – Croatian scientists are becoming more and more concerned by Adriatic Sea test results following 75 years of frequent measurements.

Scientists from the Ruđer Bošković Institute have analysed 75 years of measurements showing that the warming and salinisation of the Mediterranean Sea are accelerating, and the changes are becoming increasingly clear even in the deep layers. The Adriatic-Ionian area stands out particularly in this regard. Morski reports that when a warmer sea in summer is discussed, it usually means the temperature that is more or less suitable for swimming near the coastline itself. However, what we see and feel near the surface is only a small part of the story. Below it lie hundreds and thousands of metres of seawater, whose deep layers change much more slowly and are considerably harder to monitor.

It was precisely in these layers of the sea that scientists from the Ruđer Bošković Institute sought an answer to the question of how much the Mediterranean has really changed over the past decades. Dr Elena Terzić and Dr Ivica Vilibić, in a paper published in the leading international geoscience journal Geophysical Research Letters, collected and connected data from different periods, from historical measurements from research vessels to modern autonomous Argo floats that today regularly dive into the depths of the sea. In this manner, they obtained a kind of cross-section of the Mediterranean from 1950 to 2025 and tracked what is happening with the temperature, salinity and density of the sea at different depths. The results show that the Mediterranean is not only warming and becoming saltier, but that the speed of these changes is increasing, and their signal can be tracked hundreds and thousands of metres below the surface.

the sea’s warmth is increasing and the process is accelerating…

We have known for a long time that the sea is warming, and this process is most often described by the average rate of warming, i.e. by how much the sea temperature increases on average over one decade. “The average rate of warming tells us how much the sea temperature changed over some longer period. However, when we describe the entire period with a single average rate, we do not see whether the speed of warming itself is also changing. Our results show that it is increasing, so the average can conceal how much faster the changes of recent decades actually are,” explains Dr Elena Terzić.

In other words, a single straight line showing average warming no longer describes well enough what is happening in the Mediterranean. That is why the scientists also analysed the acceleration of warming, i.e. whether the speed at which the temperature is rising is itself changing. The clearest signal is seen near the surface, but the more interesting part of the story begins when one looks deeper. In the last years of the analysed period the temperature in the first hundred metres or so of the Mediterranean was about two degrees higher than the average of the second half of the 20th century. Warming is clearly visible also between 300 and 1,000 metres, and a measurable signal appears even at depths between one and two kilometres.

This is important because the deep sea does not react quickly to what is happening in the atmosphere. The surface can warm up during one exceptionally hot summer and cool down again a few months later, while changes in the deep sea take place much more slowly. “When the signal of change is no longer seen only near the surface but also deep in the water column, we are talking about a much broader change in the properties of the sea. The deep layers are a kind of memory of what has been happening in the system over a longer period,” emphasises Dr Ivica Vilibić.

why does the adriatic stand out here?

The temperature is not the only thing that is changing, because the Mediterranean Sea is simultaneously becoming saltier as well, especially in its central and eastern parts. Salinity and temperature together determine the density of seawater: the higher the salinity, the denser the water, and the higher the temperature, the lower the density. It is precisely the differences in density that drive the main circulation cells in the sea, i.e. the processes by which water mixes, sinks and transfers heat and salt from one part of the Mediterranean to another. Because of this, changes that begin near the surface do not necessarily stay there.

The Adriatic has a special place in this story because it is one of the areas of the Mediterranean in which dense water is formed. During cold winter periods the surface water can cool strongly, become dense enough and begin to sink. In this way the properties that the water acquired near the surface can be transferred into the deep layers of the Adriatic, and then further towards the deep Ionian Sea and the eastern Mediterranean.

The Adriatic-Ionian system in this research proved to be one of the areas with a particularly pronounced acceleration of changes. In the southern Adriatic a strong signal of accelerated warming appears even at a depth of around 1,000 metres, accompanied by simultaneous changes in salinity. This indicates that areas in which surface water sinks can be important places for the early detection and monitoring of changes that are transferred towards the interior of the sea.

how are measurements from 1950 and 2026 connected?

One of the biggest challenges in the research was to compare the properties of the sea that over the decades were not measured in the same way. In the 1950s and 1960s the data mostly came from research vessels, while today scientists have a network of Argo floats that independently pass through the water column and regularly send data on temperature and salinity. The authors therefore combined several large data sources, checked their quality and specifically tested whether the larger number of modern measurements could introduce bias into the results, i.e. artificially create the impression of acceleration. They repeated the analyses for different time periods and with different statistical approaches, and the basic pattern remained visible.

the wider mediterranean is an early indicator

The Mediterranean is a relatively small and almost closed marine basin that reacts strongly to changes in the atmosphere. Precisely for that reason it can serve scientists as a kind of natural laboratory for understanding what is happening to the oceans in a warmer climate. The research does not give a final answer to the question of which individual process is responsible for the observed acceleration. The changes can be connected with the warming of the atmosphere, evaporation and precipitation, the exchange of water with the Atlantic through Gibraltar, and changes in the circulation of the Mediterranean itself.

For the scientists the next step is to determine the contribution of each of these processes, and what they can already conclude is that the change in the Mediterranean is no longer only a story about a warmer sea surface. The sea is changing ever faster, and the signal of these changes has reached deep below the surface.

World.title: US dollar surges past 160,000 IQD amid US liquidity pressures and market slump
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar crossed the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency markets during opening trading on Saturday, September 19, 2026, marking a sharp depreciation of the domestic currency as market liquidity contracted under geopolitical and fiscal strains.

Bureaus in Baghdad posted selling prices of 160,000 dinars per $100 against buying rates of 159,500 dinars, while trading in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, reflected a parallel surge, settling at 159,650 dinars for sale and 159,100 dinars for purchase.

The widening spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s official peg of 131,000 dinars follows reports of heightened U.S. Treasury pressure and restrictions on monthly physical cash shipments from Iraq’s oil revenue reserves held at the U.S. Federal Reserve.

Washington has reportedly conditioned the continuity of unhindered dollar liquidity flows on Baghdad’s progress in disarming Iran-aligned armed factions and meeting the critical September 30 deadline, which coincides with the scheduled conclusion of the International Coalition’s military presence.

The resulting cash shortage has fueled market speculation, with local traders and currency dealers warning that selling rates could climb toward the 170,000-dinar mark if physical inflows remain constrained.

The monetary volatility has begun depressing consumer sentiment across the country ahead of the month-end deadline. Households across Iraqi governorates have visibly shifted toward precautionary saving and defensive spending, prioritizing essential food commodities while curtailing expenditures on discretionary goods and leisure services.

Foot traffic and commercial turnover have contracted noticeably across cafes, restaurants, and retail markets—even extending to school stationery vendors preparing for the upcoming academic term—choking domestic cash flow and deepening liquidity bottlenecks across the real economy.

World.title: Iraq Customs clarifies duties on pharmaceuticals, vitamins, and supplements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi General Authority of Customs asserted on Friday evening, September 18, 2026, that the formal classification of imported commodities and the determination of their corresponding Harmonized System (HS) codes and tariff bands remain the exclusive legal jurisdiction of the customs authority.

In a statement received IraqiNews.com, the authority clarified the operative tariff schedules for healthcare products, noting that certified pharmaceutical products are levied at a baseline duty of 0.5%, while vitamins and dietary supplements face duties of either 5% or 10% based on technical categorization.

Customs regulators emphasized that receiving testing clearances or regulatory approvals from the Ministry of Health does not automatically classify a product as a pharmaceutical medicine for border assessment purposes.

The authority underlined that health sector certifications fulfill domestic safety compliance requirements, whereas border taxation, HS code designation, and duty assessments are determined strictly through official statutory tariff tables and active customs regulations.

Under the declared tariff structure, conventional pharmaceuticals formally categorized under recognized medical subheadings qualify for the lower 0.5% rate.

Conversely, vitamins and nutritional supplements are evaluated individually based on their specific chemical formulation, physical composition, and technical commodity descriptions, subjecting them to standard 5% or 10% duty brackets rather than pharmaceutical exemptions.

The authority reiterated that brand names, marketing designations, or laboratory review bodies do not dictate tariff bands, which rely solely on technical HS documentation.

The regulatory clarification addresses recurring friction between border revenue authorities and the domestic healthcare market regarding import costs. In January 2026, the General Authority of Customs confirmed a 1% tariff adjustment on medical supplies, dismissing claims of a ten-fold duty increase flagged by the Iraqi Syndicate of Pharmacists as an unintentional clerical error.

The latest customs advisory establishes clear statutory boundaries between health testing protocols and fiscal border valuations, maintaining firm oversight over revenue collection on non-essential health and wellness supplements entering the country.

World.title: Iraqi Election Commission monitors Russian elections in Moscow
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A senior delegation from Iraq’s Independent High Electoral Commission (IHEC), headed by the Chairman of the Board of Commissioners, Judge Omar Ahmed Mohammed, commenced official international election monitoring duties in the Russian Federation on Friday, September 18, 2026.

The delegation, which includes Chief Electoral Officer Hussein Abdul-Sada Baheer and Board of Commissioners member Abbas Farhan, is participating as accredited international observers for the Russian State Duma parliamentary elections running through September 20, following a formal invitation extended by the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation.

IHEC confirmed in an official statement that the visit is designed to enhance institutional cooperation, facilitate knowledge exchange on electoral administration, and examine international frameworks for staging large-scale voting processes.

Alongside their direct oversight roles, the Iraqi delegation is taking part in the international forum entitled “Elections in Times of Turmoil,” an expert convening addressing technical, logistical, and administrative mechanisms required to organize and secure democratic balloting under exceptional operational constraints and shifting geopolitical realities.

As part of their official itinerary, the Iraqi commissioners initiated field inspection rounds across several designated polling stations to observe on-the-ground voting workflows firsthand.

The monitoring tour focused on evaluating voting machine operations, logistical organization, ballot management, and queue protocols inside voting centers. IHEC noted that participating in high-level overseas monitoring missions forms a core element of its strategy to benchmark international best practices, integrate comparative operational knowledge, and refine Iraq’s domestic technical and administrative capacities for future electoral cycles.

World.title: Iraq and France work on energy pipeline to Europe
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — France is working with Iraq and Jordan on a pipeline project to transport Iraqi oil and gas to European markets, French President Emmanuel Macron said days after Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi visited Paris for discussions on energy and investment.

Macron stated that the initiative was part of attempts to secure an alternate energy supply for Europe, since the Middle East crisis interrupts conventional shipping routes and raises oil and gas costs.

Iraqi official media said that the planned pipeline would take Iraqi energy via Jordan to European markets.

The statement comes after Al-Zaidi’s official visit to France from September 13 to 14, during which he met with Macron at the Élysée Palace.

The two leaders addressed diversifying energy supply pathways in the wake of delays to Iraqi oil shipments and increased pressure on global energy markets.

During the visit, Iraq and TotalEnergies, a French energy giant, agreed to initiate negotiations on further energy projects, including gas supply collaboration.

TotalEnergies is also looking for a share in the multinational consortium implementing the proposed Basra-Baniyas pipeline, which would give Iraqi petroleum an alternative route from southern oilfields to Syria’s Mediterranean coast, circumventing the Strait of Hormuz.

Chevron, TI Capital, and UCC Holdings of Qatar are all members of the partnership.

The projects highlight Iraq’s quickening efforts to diversify export routes after interruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which revealed the risk of depending mainly on southern marine terminals for petroleum shipments.

Macron said that Middle Eastern turmoil has exacerbated Europe’s energy challenges, making alternative oil and gas suppliers even more crucial.

France is also advocating for more international cooperation on energy stockpiles and supply, while prices stay high.

For Iraq, new pipeline links via Jordan and Syria might give alternate routes to European clients while lessening its vulnerability to outages in the Arabian Gulf.

World.title: England can build on World Cup ‘spirit’, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said England will build on the “fantastic spirit” of their World Cup campaign as he targets glory on home soil at Euro 2028.

The England boss was speaking at Wembley after naming a 27-man group for a four-game Nations League camp, starting with a clash against world champions Spain on September 26.

It comes just nine weeks after the end of the World Cup, where England conceded two late goals in a painful semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer were the headline picks after both were controversially overlooked for the World Cup.

Tuchel also included Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in his first squad since the tournament in North America.

A number of players who were in the World Cup squad including John Stones, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson and Dean Henderson missed out through injury.

Former Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Tuchel said he did not see the Nations League as a new start, instead focusing on continuity.

“I feel that it’s not a new beginning that we are starting now, so we build on a solid and very valuable foundation, and the target is to win the home Euros,” he told reporters on Friday.

Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

The German said his side’s ultimate failure at the World Cup had left him unfulfilled but stuck by his squad picks.

“I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic,” he said.

“I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.”

Tuchel said Palmer had impressed for Chelsea early in the season.

“He has his numbers back, he has assists back, he has decisive goals back, so that’s why he’s in the squad and I think he has a point to prove,” he said.

“The same goes for Trent. He was never off the list, he was never in a non-selectable class, and he has this chance to show, to be the best version of himself.”

Tuchel said it was his “duty” to play Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he failed to feature for a single minute at the World Cup.

The England boss welcomed the challenge of taking on Spain at Wembley.

“We feel the gap is closing and we feel that we are close and we want a proof of point,” he said.

“The stadium is sold out, it will be very exciting, the motivation cannot be higher to play against the world champions.”

England also play the Czech Republic twice and Croatia once during the upcoming international window.

World.title: Anti-Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
World.content:
Damascus – Syrian singer Assala Nasri has made a triumphant return to Damascus with a sold-out concert following 15 years of exile due to her opposition to ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad.

Thousands of fans welcomed the 57-year-old, known mononymously as Assala, at a venue in the Syrian capital where she bowed and opened the show with songs hailing the Syrian people.

“Souls of my heart, I missed you,” she repeatedly said to endless cheers on Thursday night.

“My loves, my people, I swear, until this moment I could not believe that I am among you. I want to tell you how much I dreamt of this.”

There was a heavy security presence for the concert, after some religious conservatives launched a campaign calling for its cancellation.

Half of the show’s proceeds will be donated to charity.

Syria’s new Islamist authorities, who overthrew Assad in 2024, have welcomed Assala. Culture Minister Mohammed Yassine Saleh has dubbed her “the daughter of Damascus”.

Joining her on stage, he said her return was that of “every honest Syrian and every free person”.

– ‘Moving forward’ –

Assala was among the first artists to express support for the peaceful anti-Assad protests that erupted in 2011, refusing to partake in events supporting his government.

She was booted from the Syrian artists’ union for her stance and was the target of media campaigns.

She went into exile, living in Cairo with her family and playing shows in various Arab countries.

The bloody repression of the protests led to a 13-year civil war that killed more than half-a-million people.

At Assala’s show, small Syrian flags rippled in time with the music, with many in the crowd unable to hold back their tears.

“I never thought this day would come. It’s like a beautiful dream,” concert-goer Sawsan Wadha, 56, said.

“We are very happy that our country is moving forward,” added 40-year-old Lynn Nahas.

On her new record, “The Syrian Album”, Assala covers folk songs from all 14 of Syria’s provinces as an homage to her country’s cultural diversity.

She sings for the cities scarred by war, but also for the coastline in mourning after last year’s killing of hundreds of members of Assad’s Alawite minority, and for Druze-majority Sweida, which also saw sectarian violence.

– Recovery through art –

Assala’s piercing, powerful voice rang out as she made her way through the album’s tracks at Thursday’s concert.

She also performed fan favourites like “Samehtak” and “Sandooq”, with the jubilant, tearful crowd singing along.

Assala and her family only returned to Damascus this week. An antiques dealer in the capital returned the oud, or Oriental lute, that had belonged to her father, a celebrated musician.

Conservative Muslim figures had expressed criticism in the run-up to the concert.

Egyptian preacher Hani Dahab, who lives in Syria, launched a social media campaign with the slogan “Cancel the Sinful Concerts”. He accused the culture ministry of seeking to “give society a secular character”.

Syrian Salafi preacher Abdul Razzaq al-Mahdi condemned what he called a “concert of music and debauchery”, while a group of preachers in Damascus called on the culture minister to take into account “the religious identity of society”.

While not addressing the critics directly, Assala said at the show that “recovery will only happen with art and music”.

Syria has seen a cultural boom since 2025, but also the rise of preachers and conservative religious movements in public spaces and at universities, raising fears of restrictions on freedom.

Farah Al-Atassi, political advisor to the government, said poetry, language and thought were “an integral part of Syrian identity”.

“This is the Syria that we know and that will endure,” she told AFP.

World.title: UNESCO can be ‘moderator’ in AI debate: chief to AFP
World.content:
Paris – UNESCO chief Khaled el-Enany has proposed in an interview with AFP that the UN culture and education agency become a facilitator in the worldwide wrangling on the risks of artificial intelligence.

“I believe we are uniquely positioned to make UNESCO a true moderator in this global debate,” he said as he prepared to welcome Pope Leo XIV, a key advocate for international AI governance, in Paris next week.

The UN educational, scientific and cultural organisation has long stressed that its remit covers more than heritage, looking to advance in areas ranging from access to education to the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

The debate over the potential dangers of self-improving algorithms has surged in recent weeks, with some researchers warning the technology could end humanity, and leaders of AI companies suggesting development needed to be slowed down.

US President Donald Trump has on the other hand called the fears a “hoax”.

Enany told AFP: “There is a risk that it will get out of control if we don’t intervene.”

“This break, this dialogue that has taken place over the past few weeks, is something very positive,” he added in the interview on Thursday.

He said the cultural agency had found an “indispensable partner” in the pontiff, who is to visit the UNESCO headquarters in Paris on Friday next week at the start of a four-day trip to France.

“This visit will be the beginning of a very solid partnership to strengthen and protect human dignity in this industrial revolution,” Enany said.

It will be the first visit by a pope to UNESCO headquarters since John Paul II in 1980.

– AI ‘must be governed’ –

Pope Leo, the first US pope, this week warned against delegating to algorithms decisions that should be taken by humans alone.

In his first major document, the encyclical “Magnifica Humanitas” (Magnificent Humanity), published in May, the pope issued a call to “disarm” AI in order to “prevent it from dominating humanity”.

Enany said UNESCO had long been concerned with regulating AI, in 2021 issuing a “Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence”.

The guide warned about the risk of violations of privacy and the concentration of technological power in the hands of a few states or companies, and well as potential effects on democracy and the environment.

AI is “an extraordinary tool, but one that must be governed in an ethical, inclusive, and fair way,” Enany said.

Trump has since returning to office withdrawn the United States from UNESCO, alleging that it is biased against Israel and promotes “divisive” causes.

China — one of the major global AI players — has become the agency’s largest donor.

Trump had already ordered a departure from UNESCO in 2017 during his first term, before President Joe Biden reestablished US membership.

As the United States rejoined in 2023, then US secretary of state Antony Blinken said it was key Washington was present at UNESCO for decisions “that actually matter”, including on “rules, norms and standards for artificial intelligence”.

China was among countries to oppose the move.

World.title: BJP promise in its coastal bastion: Why DK Shivakumar put Tulu at centre in Mangaluru
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief minister

on Friday announced that Tulu, spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, would be recognised as an additional administrative language in the region, fulfilling a long-standing demand.

"Today, we have decided to make Tulu applicable to Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts and declare it the stateâs second additional administrative language," Shivakumar told reporters after a marathon cabinet meeting in Mangaluru.

According to a cabinet note shared by the chief ministerâs office, Tulu would be Karnatakaâs "second additional administrative language" in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi.

The 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native Tulu speakers in Karnataka, whose population was recorded at over six crore at the time.

Kannada is the state's most-widely spoken and its primary official language.

This was also the first time a cabinet meeting was held in Mangaluru and not in Bengaluru.

Eye on BJP's coastal bastion

The political significance of Shivakumar taking his cabinet to Mangaluru becomes clearer against the BJP's electoral dominance in the region.

Coastal Karnataka, particularly Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, has long been one of the BJP's strongest pockets in the state.





In the 2023 Karnataka assembly election, BJP won 11 of the 13 seats across the two districts, taking all five seats in Udupi and six of the eight in Dakshina Kannada. The Congress won only two constituencies.

This was despite Congress sweeping to power across Karnataka with 135 seats, against 66 for the BJP.

The BJP's hold remained intact in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It won both parliamentary seats covering the region, with Brijesh Chowta defeating Congress's Padmaraj R by over 64,000 votes in Dakshina Kannada.

Kota Srinivas Poojary won Udupi-Chikkamagaluru by more than 2.5 lakh votes.

The BJP responded to the Tulu announcement by alleging that Shivakumar was "peddling soft Hindutva to make a dent in the BJPâs vote bank."

"Shivakumar has never made any secret of his firm belief in Hinduism and frequently visits temples, performs rituals publicly and quotes scriptures. He is now peddling soft Hindutva. This was also evident from his rendition of 'Namaste Sada Vatsale' inside the Karnataka assembly," a BJP leader told PTI, referring to an August 2025 incident in which Shivakumar sang a few lines of the RSS anthem.

The RSS is the BJP's ideological mentor.

But there is a political twist to the Tulu issue itself. The BJP had previously taken up the demand while in power in Karnataka.

In January 2023, the then BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai constituted a committee to examine granting Tulu the status of a second official language in the state, months before the assembly election.

More than just Tulu

Significantly, Shivakumarâs announcements went beyond granting Tulu the status of a second administrative language.

The Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru marked the Shivakumar governmentâs first meeting outside Bengaluru, the state capital. Shivakumar claimed the move was intended to recognise the regionâs contribution and address its development needs.

He also announced a host of policies for the coastal Karnataka region, introducing a dedicated tourism policy for the coastal areas to treats tourism projects as infrastructure initiatives while offering investors special incentives and extended loan repayment windows.

Additionally, the government approved the Karnataka Marine Biotechnology Policy, 2026-31, which paves the way for upgrading the existing fisheries college into the Fisheries, Marine and Blue Economy University and expanding its student intake from 60 to 200 seats.

World.title: DUSU election results: BJP hails ABVP's 'splendid victory'; Congress claim vote tampering
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Saturday won three of the four central panel posts in the Delhi University Students' Union election, with its candidate Yash Dabas elected president.

Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen, who was denied a ticket by the Congress-affiliated NSUI, won the vice-president's post.

BJP hails 'splendid victory'

Union home minister Amit Shah hailed the victory saying "Heartfelt congratulations to all the dedicated workers of the council on the splendid victory of in the Delhi University Students' Union elections.

This victory reflects the unwavering trust of the youth in the council's ideology of "Nation First" and its commitment to student welfare.

I am fully confident that the council's workers, drawing new energy from this victory and following the ideals of Swami Vivekananda Ji, will continue to relentlessly advance the cause of student interests and nation-building."

BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday congratulated the ABVP for its victory.

"Congratulations to all my young friends at Delhi University on ABVPâs historic victory in the DUSU elections! This victory reflects the youthâs continued faith in positive and constructive student politics, rooted in the spirit of Nation First, and their strong resolve to contribute to the vision of a âViksit Bharatâ.





My best wishes to the victorious candidates and everyone who worked tirelessly to make this victory possible," Nabin said in a post on X.

Defence minister Rajnath Singh also congratulated the ABVP on its victory in the Delhi University Students' Union elections.

"Heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all workers on the splendid success of @ABVPVoice in the Delhi University Students' Union elections. This victory is a symbol of the unwavering faith of the youth in the Nation First policy.

I am confident that ABVP will continue to work with the same dedication in commitment to student interests, national service, and nation-building. Heartfelt congratulations to the entire ABVP team and best wishes for a bright future!" the defence minister said in a post on X.

World.title: Mamata's 72-hour rollercoaster: Losing symbol, TMC name, candidate and then a breather on Day 3
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Once the dominant political force in West Bengal, Mamata Banerjee-led

is facing an unusual stretch of turbulence. Questions over the party's identity, leadership and organisational cohesion have all surfaced in the space of just 72 hours.

For years, Mamata and the TMC have been almost synonymous in Bengal politics. But the past three days have brought one jolt after another, leaving the party dealing with a frozen identity, a new name and symbol, a candidate walking away in Nandigram and another nearly doing the same in Rejinagar.

Day 1: EC freezes TMC name and symbol

The first shock came when the

froze the TMC's familiar party name and its traditional 'flowers-and-grass' symbol amid the battle between

and the rival faction led by Arup Roy.

The move was more than a technical setback for a party whose name and symbol have been central to its electoral identity for years.

It also came after Mamata's stinging defeat at the hands of the

BJP

in the assembly polls, leaving the party vulnerable to rebellion and splits in both the state assembly and Parliament.

The rebel faction had sought to stake its claim over the TMC's identity after 15 straight years of the party's rule in Bengal.





Day 2: New name, new symbol, then Nandigram shock

The next day brought some clarity, but hardly any comfort for Didi.

The Election Commission allotted the 'footballer' symbol to Mamata's faction and the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress'. The rival faction led by once-a-Didi-loyalist Arup Roy was given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol.

However, the drama for Didi went ahead to Nandigram seat.

Sanchita Pradhan Dey, the TMC candidate in Nandigram, withdrew her nomination a day before the deadline after meeting Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, the BJP leader who had defeated Mamata in Nandigram.

Dey, who had lost her job in connection with the teacher recruitment scam, met Adhikari along with her husband Satyajit before announcing her withdrawal. Her reasons were not immediately clear.

The development left Mamata scrambling for a candidate in a constituency that is considered a Suvendu Adhikari bastion.

Mamata then backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan and described Congress as a "sister party", a move that also brought the INDIA bloc back into the picture ahead of the October 6 bypolls.

But the reprieve was short-lived.

Hours later, Milan Pradhan was arrested in connection with criminal cases linked to the 2007 anti-land acquisition movement in Nandigram, Purba Medinipur.

The Mamata camp accused the BJP government of "acting in an authoritarian manner to crush dissent and win the bypoll by a huge margin".

BJP leader and Union minister Sukanta Majumdar said such allegations were expected from a "party centred on one person, whose activists had carried out attacks on the then opposition BJP after the 2021 assembly polls".

Day 3: Rejinagar brings another scare, then a breather

Just when the Nandigram episode seemed to have given Mamata enough to deal with, Rejinagar produced another surprise.

Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the TMC candidate and former MLA, announced that he would withdraw from the bypoll, citing difficulties in motivating grassroots workers, police arrests and what he described as false cases against party workers. He also said familiarising voters with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time was proving difficult.

"It is becoming difficult for me to motivate grassroots workers who have been facing regular harassment. Police have arrested many of our workers, slapping false cases. Also, it is an onerous task to familiarise the electorate with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time. In this given situation, I informed Mamata di last evening about my decision (not to contest)... Let's see," he said.

But within about 1.5 hours, the withdrawal itself was withdrawn.

"I will be contesting the bypoll. We are in Didi's party and we cannot do anything outside her wishes. So, following Didi's instructions, I am retaining my candidature," Chowdhury said.

He said Mamata had directed him not to quit. He later visited Beldanga police station and said the police had assured him and his workers of security.

"I have been assured of security by the police after the supremo (Mamata) intervened.

I have met officers of the Beldanga police station and they have also assured me and my cadre of security during campaigning," he said.

"Even if only 10 workers stand by me, I will take them along and begin a door-to-door campaign," he said.

For Mamata, it offered a small breather after two days of turbulence.

The troubling sequence unfolded over 72 hours, turning into an unsettling rollercoaster for Didi.

World.title: 'Danger to India not from communism, but Hindu right-wing communalism': Ansari cites Nehru; BJP hits back
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former vice president Mohammad Hamid Ansari on Saturday cited former prime minister

's remarks about the âdanger to Indiaâ while referring to concerns raised by late constitutional expert and author AG Noorani in his book The

: A Menace to India.

He was addressing the event, titled âRemembering a Polymath: The Life and Times of Abdul Ghafoor Nooraniâ, organised at the India Islamic Cultural Centre to commemorate the life and works of the jurist and author.

Addressing an event, Ansari recalled jurist and author Abdul Ghafoor Noorani's observations in the introduction to his 2019 book and cited remarks by Nehru that were recorded by former Foreign Secretary Jagat Singh Gundevia during a meeting of Ministry of External Affairs officials.

âThe RSS: A Menace to Indiaâ was the title of the book published in 2019. The opening lines of the introduction, where A.G. Noorani used a couplet, reflected what he described as the prevailing sentiment among Muslims in India today. In the same introduction, he referred to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehruâs remarks at a Ministry of External Affairs officersâ meeting, documented by Foreign Secretary Gundevia.





Nehru had warned that âthe real danger to India was not communism, but Hindu right-wing communalismâ," he said.

During his speech, Ansari discussed Noorani's writings and his views on nationalism, identity and political developments in India. He also referred to Noorani's criticism of what he saw as a shift from civic nationalism towards cultural nationalism.

âIn recent years, we have experienced the emergence of trends and practices that dispute the well-established principle of civic nationalism and interpose a new and imaginary practice of cultural nationalism,â Ansari said.

âIt seeks to present an electoral majority in the guise of a religious majority and monopolise political power. It wants to distinguish citizens based on their faith, give vent to intolerance, insinuate otherness, and promote disquiet and insecurity,â he added.

Ansari raised concerns over what he described as emerging trends that challenge the principle of civic nationalism.

During his speech, Ansari said, âSome of its recent manifestations are chilling and reflect poorly on our claim to be governed by the rule of law.

Itâs a question that has to be answered. These trends need to be contested and contested legally and contested politically.â

'Congressâs anti-Hindu politics in the spotlight', says BJP

Reacting to Ansari's remarks, the BJP Scheduled Tribe Morcha said the statement brought what it described as Congress's âanti-Hindu politicsâ into focus. The BJP unit also referred to Rahul Gandhi's past remarks on Hindu groups and terrorism, alleging that such statements reflected a pattern in the party's political narrative.

World.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella hails Seattle’s tech growth, deepening India ties at 'IDEAS4INDIA' forum
World.content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella praised Seattle's growing technology ecosystem and its deepening ties with India while addressing more than 40 Indian-origin tech CEOs and CTOs from across sectors, including artificial intelligence, quantum computing and enterprise software.

Nadella was the guest of honour at the first 'IDEAS4INDIA: Indian American Tech CEOs Forum | Unlocking the Tech Dividend', organised by the Consulate General of India in Seattle under Consul General Prakash Gupta.

Consul General of India Prakash Gupta delivering welcome remarks.

The forum, held Thursday at the consulate premises, followed the India AI Impact Summit held in New Delhi in February. It brought together Indian-American technology leaders from the Greater Seattle area to discuss ways to strengthen the India-US technology partnership.

Addressing the event, Nadella said he was proud to have watched the Seattle technology community grow over roughly 35 years and was pleased to see it forming and strengthening its relationship with India, the consulate said.

He described artificial intelligence as a general-purpose technology whose benefits would depend on its broad diffusion across countries, communities and sectors.

CEO and Chairman of Microsoft, Satya Nadella hails Seattleâs tech growth.

The forum brought together technology leaders working across AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, cloud infrastructure, aerospace and enterprise software.





Participants included executives from Microsoft, Amazon, Boeing, OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel, Veeam Software, Helion, Rhythms AI, Zenoti, Anicca Data and SeekOut, among others. Ajay Bhatt, the inventor of USB-C and a former Intel executive, also participated in the discussions.

India's ambassador to the US Vinay Kwatra welcomed the participants' interest in deepening the India-US technology partnership.

Kwatra reaffirmed the government's commitment to ensuring that India's AI Mission remains anchored in "inclusivity, openness, sovereignty, democratized access, safety and trust".

Ambassador Vinay Kwatra welcomed participants' interest in deepening India-US tech ties.

During an interactive session, the technology executives shared ideas on strengthening cooperation in areas including AI infrastructure, data centres, semiconductor design and manufacturing, quantum research, talent and skilling, aerospace and advanced manufacturing.

The discussions also highlighted the two-way nature of the technology relationship, with several companies represented at the forum maintaining significant engineering, research and business operations in India.

The consulate said the forum is expected to become an important platform for strengthening India-US technology ties, including under the India-US TRUST Initiative (Transforming the Relationship Utilising Strategic Technology).

Under the initiative, the two countries are working to connect their innovation ecosystems and advance collaboration in artificial intelligence, quantum technology, semiconductors, space, telecommunications and biotechnology.

Several US technology companies have also announced major investments in India.

Microsoft has announced an investment of $17.5 billion in India between 2026 and 2029, its largest investment in Asia, to expand cloud and AI infrastructure, skilling and operations.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Amazon has announced a $48 billion investment between 2026 and 2030, including an expansion of AWS data centre capacity in Mumbai and Hyderabad. Costco is also setting up its first Global Capability Centre in Hyderabad, the consulate said.

A moment of silence.

The event began with a minute's silence to honour two Indian-origin technology leaders from Seattle who recently died, Samir Bodas, co-founder and CEO of Icertis, and S Somasegar, managing director at Madrona Venture Group and former corporate vice president at Microsoft.

They were remembered for their contributions to Seattle's technology ecosystem and their support for Indian-origin startups.

The Seattle Consulate described the gathering as a first-of-its-kind forum for Indian-American technology leaders in the region.

World.title: ‘We do not operate under pressure from any nation’: Govt on Trump's Russia sanctions bill
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India will take decisions in the best interests of its people and will continue to follow an independent foreign policy, minister of state for external affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said while responding to a question on the Russian Sanctions Bill and its possible impact on India.

âThe people of India are the top priority for our government. We will take every measure that benefits our public,â Singh said while talking to ANI.

âWe act in best interests of our countryâ

Singh said India does not base its decisions on the dictates of other nations and will take steps to safeguard the country's strength and stability.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âWe will take decisive steps to ensure the strength and stability of our nation and its population. We maintain an independent foreign policy; we do not align ourselves based on the dictates of other nations but rather act in the best interests of our own country,â he said.

He also reiterated India's position on the tariffs being imposed, saying, âWe have consistently maintained that the tariffs being imposed are unfair, and we do not operate under pressure from any other nation.â

Energy remains âprimary concernâ
